title.narrative: PERFORMANCE-BASED PARTNERSHIP SCHEME FOCUSING ON QUALITY PROGRAMMING, UNDERSTANDING CHANGE AND RESULTS FOR POOR HOUSEHOLDS AND COMMUNITIES

description.narrative: In Year 3, ICSP strengthened community and district‑level health and WASH systems in Agago and Namayingo, contributing to the programme’s overall reach of 377,090 people, including 18,855 persons with disabilities. Service quality improved, with 18 of 20 facilities (90%) meeting standards and utilisation rising to 0.96. Community vulnerability reduced through improved health and nutrition practices, with 81% adopting recommended behaviours. ANC4 attendance reached 51%, immunisation 89%, and modern contraception 57%. Preparedness advanced through contingency planning, with 36,685 people covered by early action for health impacts. Health‑resilience scores reached 64.9, demonstrating stronger readiness for health‑related shocks.. Social Behaviour Change (SBC) approaches are used to build community and household capacity to care for their own health – including Care Groups, Men’s Health Groups, and community based reproductive health volunteers who work to increase the demand for health services.
